labels.label: bzthm:c3s5t1prime_reunion_convexes_sphere

hypotheses.paper: W un corps convexe de S(n)
hypotheses.here: carried (IsCorpsConvexeS n W); weakened in reunion_convexes_sphere_of_isCompact
hypotheses.note: only IsStrictConvexPart W and IsCompact W are used; the nonempty interior is never used

hypotheses.paper: V une partie compacte convexe non vide de W
hypotheses.note: IsCompact V, IsConvexPart V, V.Nonempty, V ⊆ W

hypotheses.paper: I'(V, W) : W − V est convexe
hypotheses.note: ProprieteIS V W := V ⊆ W ∧ IsConvexPart V ∧ IsConvexPart (W \ V), as the strict affine ProprieteI; the first two conjuncts are hypotheses of the theorem

hypotheses.paper: II'(V, W) : hémisphères ouverts ... système fondamental de voisinages
hypotheses.note: ProprieteIIS (every open O ⊇ V of S(E) has an open hemisphere H ⊇ V of a non-zero continuous form with H ∩ W ⊆ O), proved equivalent to the printed 'système fondamental' form: proprieteIIS_iff_systemeFondamental

hypotheses.paper: III'(V, W) : le support de V est une variété d'appui L de W, V = W ∩ H, H un hémisphère de L
hypotheses.note: support = supportK V, variété d'appui = IsVarieteAppuiK (Déf. 6), H = L ∩ closedHemisphere l with l not identically zero on F(L) (DemiSphereFermeeDe); no 'éventuellement H = L' case is needed

findings: benzecri1960_ch3.tex:1399-1411 (Th. 1′): true as printed, in every dimension n ≥ 0, when « un hémisphère H de L » (l.1410) is a CLOSED hemisphere of L; the parenthesis « éventuellement H ∩ W = L ∩ W » that the affine III carries (l.1390-1391) is rightly absent: W ∩ L lies in the genuine closed hemisphere ℓ ≥ 0 of L (ℓ > 0 on F(W)), so V = W ∩ L is reached by a genuine hemisphere (the planner's conjecture (a) is proved). Under the reading OPEN hemisphere, I′ ⇒ III′ is false: the closed half x₁ ≤ x₀ of the closed triangle of S(2) has I′ but is W ∩ L ∩ H for no open hemisphere H (Benzecri.ReunionSphereInstance.demiTriangle_sans_hemisphereOuvert). III′ ⇒ I′ holds in every reading (Benzecri.Sphere.proprieteIS_of_proprieteIIISlarge).

benzecri1960_ch3.tex:1399: unlike the affine Theorem 1 (strict reunion_convexes_dimZero, false for E = 0), Theorem 1′ holds for n = 0 as well: the affine chart of the proof is used here as the section ℓ = 1 inside ℝⁿ⁺¹ ≠ 0, and S(0) has open hemispheres.

benzecri1960_ch3.tex:1399: « corps convexe » is more than the proof uses: Theorem 1′ holds for W any compact strict convex part of S(n) (Benzecri.reunion_convexes_sphere_of_isCompact), the nonempty interior being unused (also by the strict IsCorpsConvexeS.exists_forall_pos, whose proof is reused here).

benzecri1960_ch3.tex:1414-1418 (proof): the transfer « dans cet espace, le théorème 1′ est un corollaire du théorème 1 » is not immediate: convexity, compactness, set difference, open hemispheres ↔ open half-spaces and the variétés d'appui must each be transported through the chart; formalized here (isConvexPart_iff_convex_coneSection, coneSection_sdiff, isCompact_coneSection, proprieteII_coneSection_iff, affineSpan_kPrime, proprieteI_kPrime_iff). The III′ part is transported through the cone F(·) ∪ {O} rather than the chart.
The transcription of Th. 1′ (l.1399-1411) was compared with the page image (PDF p. 53, journal p. 280): it matches.
questions: « un hémisphère H de L » (l.1410): open or closed? Reading taken: a closed hemisphere L ∩ closedHemisphere l, l not identically zero on F(L) (the planner's reading (a)). Under it the label is proved in full; under the open reading it is false (demiTriangle_sans_hemisphereOuvert). The label is left unmarked until the author rules; if the closed reading is ruled, the mark needs no code change.

II′ (l.1405-1407): read as the strict ProprieteII is (OQ-165 reading): for every open O ⊇ V an open hemisphere H ⊇ V with H ∩ W ⊆ O; proved equivalent to the printed 'système fondamental de voisinages' (proprieteIIS_iff_systemeFondamental), so this reading is not load-bearing.
« hémisphère ouvert » (l.1405): read as openHemisphere of a non-zero (continuous, automatic on S(n)) form, DEC-114.

instances: Benzecri.ReunionSphereInstance.demiTriangle_proprietes: the closed half x₁ ≤ x₀ of the closed triangle simplexS 2 of S(2) has I′, II′ and III′ (the roadmap asked for a half spherical cap; the half triangle plays the same role and reuses the strict isCorpsConvexeS_simplexS)
Benzecri.ReunionSphereInstance.vertex_proprietes: the vertex s(e₀) of the closed triangle has I′, II′ and III′

Benzecri.ReunionSphereInstance.demiSphereFermeeDe_univ (DemiSphereFermeeDe), demiSphereDe_univ (DemiSphereDe), demiTriangle_proprieteIIISlarge (ProprieteIIISlarge), simplexS_proprieteIIISouvert (ProprieteIIISouvert: V = W = the triangle, cut out by the open hemisphere ∑ xᵢ > 0), demiTriangle_proprieteIS (ProprieteIS)
kb_proposals: Chapter3/ReunionConvexesSphere: to transfer an affine § 5 statement to S(n), use the section coneSection W ℓ (ℓ > 0 on F W) for anything topological (compactness, II) and the cone kPrime for anything about supports and variétés d'appui (affineSpan_kPrime: affineSpan (kPrime V) = (span F V).toAffineSubspace; proprieteI_kPrime_iff); isConvexPart_iff_convex_coneSection is the convexity bridge.
exists_forall_pos_of_isCompact / exists_mul_norm_le_of_isCompact: the strict IsCorpsConvexeS lemmas hold for any compact strict convex part (resp. nonempty compact part); the interior is never used.
A half-space L ∩ {f ≤ c} of a vector subspace meeting a convex cone in a cone is L ∩ {f ≤ 0}: closed half-spaces of the cone picture become closed hemispheres (proof of proprieteIIIS_of_proprieteIS).
